title: 7 活的箭活的藤8 路遇劫匪
content_zh:
还有，树会发光，这正常吗？
一念及此，他带着疑问开口道：“发光？是树本身，还是因为其它什么原因？”
“是树本身！
它叫夜光木，它的树皮会在夜里发出淡蓝色的光。
夜里看过去，整座山星星点点……平常时候，毛鲁人会把它的皮剥下来，贴在经常活动的地方，不用点灯也能看见。”
曹笔想象着那个画面。
蓝色的光，幽暗的山林，有点像阿凡达啊。
“毛鲁人长什么样？”
“毛鲁人比咱们矮小，但精壮。
他们的皮肤是褐色的，眼珠子是黑的，但瞳孔比咱们大，夜里能看清东西。
据说是因为常年在山林里钻，眼睛进化成了那样。
因为这个原因，他们族群中有很大一部分，喜欢白天休息，夜间活动。”
“他们休息的地方也比较特别，跟我们和凶骨族都不一样。
他们住树上，住在一种叫藤屋的东西里。
藤屋一般离地三四丈，不爬上去根本看不见。
他们进出都靠藤梯，白天收起来，晚上放下去，外人根本找不到。”
曹笔想了想，感觉有点像吊脚楼的高配版。
“对了，毛鲁人崇拜灵。”
周娘子似乎想到了什么：“他们相信山里的每一棵树，每一根藤，每一块石头里都住着灵。
所以进山之前要祭祀，砍树之前要祷告，猎到猎物要留下一部分献给山灵。

如果不敬，就会被灵诅咒，在山里迷路，永远走不出来……”
“……毛鲁人打仗，也跟咱们不一样。”
周娘子见曹笔听得认真，便继续往下说。
“他们几乎不列阵，也不硬拼。
官军进山围剿，他们就在林子里跟咱们捉迷藏。
明明听见周围都是他们的声音，可就是看不见人。
等咱们累了，停下休息，冷不丁一支箭从树上射下来，人就没了。”
“他们用什么武器？”
“弓箭为主。”
周娘子说：“弓不大，但力道足，近距离能射穿皮甲。
箭头是用一种叫毒棘的植物汁液淬过的，射中了伤口发黑发烂，没有相应的解药，很难处理。
还有一种箭，箭头是活的。”
“活的？”
“嗯，有一种寄生在树上的虫子，拇指大小，背上长着硬刺。
毛鲁人把虫子装在竹筒里，射箭的时候连虫带箭一起射出去。
箭扎进肉里，虫子就往肉里钻，一边钻一边产卵，几天功夫，伤口里就全是蛆。”
曹笔眉头动了动，不由自主脑补那个画面。
“除了弓箭，他们还用陷阱。”
周娘子继续说：“山里到处都是他们挖的坑，插着削尖的木桩，上面铺树叶，一脚踩空人就没了。
还有用藤蔓做的绊索，绊倒了吊起来，挂在半空中等人来收。”

她顿了顿，又道：“最可怕的一种陷阱，叫血藤坑。
content_en:
Also, the tree will glow, is this normal?
Thinking of this, he asked with doubt: "Glowing? Is it the tree itself, or is it due to some other reason?"
“It’s the tree itself!
It's called luminous wood, and its bark emits light blue light at night.
Looking at it at night, the whole mountain is dotted with stars... Usually, the Maulu people will peel off its skin and stick it in places where they often move, so that they can be seen without lighting a lamp. "
Cao Bi imagined that scene.
The blue light and dark mountain forest are a bit like Avatar.
“What do Mauru people look like?”
"The Mauru people are shorter than us, but stronger.
Their skin is brown and their eyes are black, but their pupils are larger than ours and they can see clearly at night.
It is said that the eyes evolved like this due to being in the mountains and forests all year round.
For this reason, a large part of their group likes to rest during the day and be active at night. "
“The place where they rest is also quite special, it’s different from us and the Fierce Bone Clan.
They live in trees, in something called a vine house.
The vine house is usually three to four feet above the ground and cannot be seen unless you climb up.
They use rattan ladders to get in and out. They put them up during the day and put them down at night, so outsiders can't find them. "
Cao Bi thought about it and felt a bit like a high-end version of Diaojiaolou.
"By the way, the Mauru people worship spirits."
Mrs. Zhou seemed to have thought of something: "They believe that every tree, every vine, and every stone in the mountains has a spirit living in it.
Therefore, you must offer sacrifices before entering the mountains, pray before cutting down trees, and leave part of the prey you hunt to offer to the mountain spirits.
If you are disrespectful, you will be cursed by the spirit, get lost in the mountains, and never come out..."
"...The Maulu people also fight differently from us."
Seeing that Cao Bi was listening carefully, Mrs. Zhou continued.
“They hardly line up and don’t push hard.
When the officers and soldiers entered the mountains to encircle and suppress us, they would hide and seek with us in the woods.
I could clearly hear their voices all around, but I couldn't see anyone.
When we got tired and stopped to rest, suddenly an arrow shot down from the tree and everyone was gone. "
"What weapons did they use?"
"The main thing is bows and arrows."
Madam Zhou said: "The bow is not big, but it is powerful and can shoot through leather armor at close range.
The arrowhead was quenched with the juice of a plant called poisonous thorn. The wound turned black and rotten when it was shot. There was no corresponding antidote and it was difficult to treat.
There is also a kind of arrow whose arrowhead is alive. "
"Alive?"
"Well, there is a parasitic insect that lives on trees. It is about the size of a thumb and has hard thorns on its back.
The Maulu people put insects in bamboo tubes and shoot out the insects and arrows together when shooting arrows.
When the arrow pierces the flesh, the insects burrow into the flesh, laying eggs as they burrow. Within a few days, the wound is filled with maggots. "
Cao Bi's brows moved, and he couldn't help but imagine that scene.
"In addition to bows and arrows, they also use traps."
Mrs. Zhou continued: "There are pits dug by them everywhere in the mountains, with sharpened wooden stakes inserted and leaves spread on them. The people would be gone when they stepped on them.
There are also trip wires made of vines, which can be hoisted up if someone trips over them, hanging in mid-air waiting for someone to collect them. "
She paused and then said: "The most terrifying trap is called the Blood Vine Pit.
